title: Module Assessment: Design Patterns & Architecture (PY_258 to PY_264)

slides.title: Module 9 Overview
slides.prompt: Assessment covering Creational, Structural, and Behavioral Design Patterns, Dependency Injection, and Enterprise Architecture Principles in Python.

slides.title: Question 1: Singleton Pattern
slides.prompt: What is the primary objective of the Singleton Design Pattern?
options: To ensure a class has only one instance and provides a global point of access to it
To create a factory for generating family objects
To convert the interface of a class into another interface
To separate object construction from its representation
slides.correctAnswer: To ensure a class has only one instance and provides a global point of access to it

slides.title: Question 2: Singleton Implementation
slides.prompt: Fill in the magic method used to control instance creation in Python for Singleton implementation.

slides.title: Question 3: Factory Method Pattern
slides.prompt: Which design pattern defines an interface for creating an object, but lets subclasses decide which class to instantiate?

slides.title: Question 4: Adapter Pattern
slides.prompt: Which pattern acts as a wrapper to allow incompatible interfaces to work together?

slides.title: Question 5: Observer Pattern
slides.prompt: Fill in the architectural pattern name where an object maintains a list of dependents and notifies them automatically of state changes.

slides.title: Question 6: Strategy Pattern
slides.prompt: Which pattern enables selecting an algorithm's behavior at runtime by encapsulating interchangeable algorithms?

slides.title: Question 7: Decorator Pattern vs Decorators
slides.prompt: How does the structural Decorator Pattern relate to Python's language-level `@decorator` feature?
options: Python decorators dynamically add behavior to functions/classes, directly implementing the Decorator Pattern
They are completely unrelated concepts in software architecture
Python decorators can only be applied to static methods
Decorator pattern strictly requires inheritance while Python decorators use memory pools
slides.correctAnswer: Python decorators dynamically add behavior to functions/classes, directly implementing the Decorator Pattern

slides.title: Question 8: SOLID Principles - D
slides.prompt: Fill in the term: Dependency ___ Principle states high-level modules should not depend on low-level modules; both should depend on abstractions.

slides.title: Question 9: Facade Pattern
slides.prompt: What does the Facade pattern provide in complex software systems?
options: A simplified, unified interface to a complex subsystem
A mechanism to clone objects without coupling to their classes
A way to pass requests along a chain of handlers
An interface for stepping through a complex data structure
slides.correctAnswer: A simplified, unified interface to a complex subsystem

slides.title: Question 10: Proxy Pattern
slides.prompt: Which pattern provides a surrogate or placeholder object to control access to another target object?

slides.title: Question 11: Dependency Injection
slides.prompt: Fill in the design pattern practice where dependent services are passed into an object during instantiation rather than hardcoded.

slides.title: Question 12: Command Pattern
slides.prompt: Which behavioral pattern encapsulates a request as an object, allowing parameterization and undoable operations?

slides.title: Question 13: Repository Pattern
slides.prompt: In Enterprise Architecture, what is the role of the Repository Pattern?
options: To mediate between the domain and data mapping layers using a collection-like interface
To cache API responses at the network boundary
slides.correctAnswer: To mediate between the domain and data mapping layers using a collection-like interface

slides.title: Question 14: Borg Pattern (Pythonic Singleton Alternative)
slides.prompt: Fill in the attribute modified in the Borg pattern to share state across all instances instead of identity.
